title.value: Global Variations in Event-Based Surveillance for Disease Outbreak Detection: Time Series Analysis
title.justification: The title encapsulates the main focus of the paper which is the analysis of variations in event-based surveillance across different global regions for disease outbreak detection.
title.quote: Global Variations in Event-Based Surveillance for Disease Outbreak Detection: Time Series Analysis

extractions.description: This study evaluates the performance variations of event-based surveillance systems, HealthMap and Epidemic Intelligence from Open Sources (EIOS), in detecting disease outbreaks globally, using influenza as a case. It seeks to identify country-specific factors determining these variations and discusses the implications for public health surveillance, especially in low and middle-income countries.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper primarily focuses on evaluating the performance of event-based surveillance systems in detecting disease outbreaks. While public health is an important aspect of sustainable development, the paper does not directly address climate or ecological sustainable development issues.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: The aim of this study was to assess the variation in the timing and frequency of EBS reports compared to true outbreaks and to identify the determinants of variability by using the example of seasonal influenza epidemic in 24 countries.

primary_category.justification: The closest related field in this context is Climate Science, particularly because the study involves modeling and analysis of data systems like surveillance, which could tangentially connect to prediction systems in climate science.
primary_category.quote: Objective: The aim of this study was to assess the variation in the timing and frequency of EBS reports compared to true outbreaks and to identify the determinants of variability by using the example of seasonal influenza epidemic in 24 countries.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper discusses the need for improved surveillance systems particularly in low and resource-limited settings, which aligns with supporting the Global South in health infrastructure.
secondary_categories.quote: Therefore, advances in the development and evaluation and EBS are needed, particularly in low-resource settings.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper aligns with the idea of risks modeling when it deals with outbreak detection and prediction methodologies, although it is not directly related to climate risks.
primary_sub_category.quote: Infectious disease surveillance produces crucial information for public health professionals to make good emergency response decisions and implement effective countermeasures to contain outbreaks.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Although the paper doesn't directly deal with climate data, its theme of handling large datasets in the context of public health surveillance has parallels with managing climate data.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Data: In addition to early disease activity detection, surveillance for events has the potential to augment the sensitivity of IBS in regions with few medical centers or lower health-seeking behaviors.

applications.justification: The primary application discussed is using surveillance systems to track and detect outbreaks of diseases like influenza.
applications.quote: Event-based surveillance (EBS) was developed to allow timely detection of infectious disease outbreaks by using mostly web-based data.

new_primary_category.justification: The existing categories encompass the themes discussed in the paper; creating a new category is unnecessary.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The existing sub-categories sufficiently describe the paper's focus areas.
